key_insight: The paper defines a Reynolds-like control parameter that predicts when active turbulence enters a universal regime, regardless of whether the transition is driven by activity, advection, saturation, or instability tuning.
engineering_relevance: This gives designers of active-matter and bacterial-flow models a single threshold metric to anticipate onset of universal turbulence and compare different control strategies on the same scale.
method: Identify the independent dimensionless groups in the Toner–Tu–Swift–Hohenberg dynamics.
Combine them into a Reynolds-like organizing parameter based on the balance of nonlinear transport and saturation.
Calibrate one critical threshold from the known activity-driven transition and test whether it predicts other routes to universality.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the same critical value collapses multiple parameter routes onto a common threshold and correctly predicts the onset of the universal $E(k)\sim k^{-3/2}$ state.
watch_item: The threshold is calibrated from one known transition, so its robustness may depend on the model class and parameter ranges considered.
paper_title: A Reynolds-like Criterion for the Onset of Universal Active Turbulence
